verses.1:1: James, a servant of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes that are in the dispersion: greetings.
verses.1:2: Regard it as all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various trials,
verses.1:3: knowing that the testing of your faith produces patience.
verses.1:4: Now patience has a perfect work, so that you may be perfect and whole, falling short in nothing.
verses.1:5: But if anyone among you lacks wisdom, let him ask from God, who gives to all abundantly and does not reproach, and it will be given to him.
verses.1:6: Yet let him ask in faith, not hesitating at all; for the one who hesitates is like a wave of the sea that is stirred by the wind and tossed about.
verses.1:7: Therefore let that man not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord.
verses.1:8: A man double in mind is unstable in all his ways.
verses.1:9: Now let the humble brother boast in his exaltation,
verses.1:10: and the rich man in his lowliness, because like a flower of grass he will pass away;
verses.1:11: for the sun has risen with scorching heat and dried up the grass, and its flower has fallen off, and the beauty of its appearance has perished; so too will the rich man fade away in his journeys.
verses.1:12: Blessed is the man who endures trial, because when he has been proved he will receive the crown of life, which God promised to those who love Him.
verses.1:13: Let no one, when tempted, say that he is tempted by God; for God is no tempter of evils, and He Himself tempts no one.
verses.1:14: But each one is tempted, drawn away and lured by his own desire.
verses.1:15: Then desire, when it has conceived, gives birth to sin; and sin, when it has been completed, brings forth death.
verses.1:16: Therefore do not go astray, my most beloved brothers.
verses.1:17: Every best bestowal and every perfect gift is from above, descending from the Father of lights, with whom there is no shifting nor shadow of alternation.
verses.1:18: For willingly He brought us forth by the word of truth, so that we might be a kind of beginning of His creation.
verses.1:19: You know, my most beloved brothers. Now let every person be swift to listen, yet slow to speak and slow to anger.
verses.1:20: For a man's anger does not produce God's righteousness.
verses.1:21: For this reason, casting off all uncleanness and abundance of malice, receive in gentleness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
verses.1:22: And be doers of the word, and not merely listeners, deceiving your very selves.
verses.1:23: Because if anyone is a listener of the word and not a doer, this one will be compared to a man examining the face of his birth in a mirror;
verses.1:24: for he examined himself and went away, and at once forgot what sort of person he was.
verses.1:25: But the one who looks deeply into the perfect law of liberty and remains in it, not having become a forgetful listener but a doer of the work, this one will be blessed in his deed.
verses.1:26: Now if anyone supposes himself to be religious, not bridling his tongue but misleading his own heart, this one's religion is empty.
verses.1:27: Religion clean and unstained before God and the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their tribulation, and to keep oneself unstained from this world.
verses.2:1: My brothers, do not hold with favoritism the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ of glory.
verses.2:2: For if a man wearing a gold ring, in bright clothing, enters your assembly, and a poor man in filthy attire also enters,
verses.2:3: and you pay attention to the one who is dressed in splendid clothing and say to him, "You sit comfortably here," while to the poor man you say, "You stand over there, or sit under my footstool,"
verses.2:4: do you not pass judgment among yourselves, and have you not become judges with wicked thoughts?
verses.2:5: Listen, my most beloved brothers: did God not choose the poor in this world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom that God promised to those who love Him?
verses.2:6: But you have dishonored the poor man. Do the rich not oppress you through power and themselves drag you into the courts?
verses.2:7: Do they themselves not blaspheme the good name that has been invoked over you?
verses.2:8: If, however, you fulfill the royal law according to the Scriptures, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you do well;
verses.2:9: but if you show favoritism, you commit sin, convicted by the law as transgressors.
verses.2:10: Now whoever keeps the entire law, yet stumbles in one thing, has become guilty of all.
verses.2:11: For He who said, "You shall not commit adultery," also said, "You shall not kill." Now if you do not commit adultery, yet you kill, you have become a transgressor of the law.
verses.2:12: Speak in this way and act in this way, as those about to be judged through the law of liberty.
verses.2:13: For judgment without mercy is for the one who has not shown mercy; yet mercy rises high above judgment.
verses.2:14: What will it profit, my brothers, if someone says he has faith, yet does not have works? Will faith be able to save him?
verses.2:15: Now if a brother and a sister are naked and lack daily food,
verses.2:16: and one of you says to them, "Go in peace, be warmed and satisfied," yet you do not give them the things necessary for the body, what will it profit?
verses.2:17: In the same way faith too, if it does not have works, is dead in itself.
verses.2:18: But someone will say, "You have faith, and I have works." Show me your faith without works, and I will show you my faith by works.
verses.2:19: You believe that there is one God; you do well. The demons also believe, and they shudder.
verses.2:20: Now do you want to know, you empty man, that faith without works is dead?
verses.2:21: Was our father Abraham not justified by works, offering his son Isaac on the altar?
verses.2:22: Do you see that faith was working together with his works, and by works faith was completed?
verses.2:23: And the Scripture was fulfilled, saying, "Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness," and he was called a friend of God.
verses.2:24: Do you see that a person is justified by works and not by faith only?
verses.2:25: Likewise, was Rahab the prostitute not also justified by works, receiving the messengers and sending them out by another way?
verses.2:26: For just as a body without spirit is dead, so too faith without works is dead.
verses.3:1: Do not let many of you become teachers, my brothers, knowing that you receive a greater judgment.
verses.3:2: For in many things we all stumble. If anyone does not stumble in word, this one is a perfect man; he is also able to lead the whole body around with a bridle.
verses.3:3: Now if we put bridles into the mouths of horses so that they comply with us, we also turn about their whole body.
verses.3:4: Look at ships too: although they are large and are driven by strong winds, they are turned about by a small rudder wherever the impulse of the one steering wills.
verses.3:5: So also the tongue is indeed a small member, and it exalts great things. Look how small a fire sets ablaze how large a forest!
verses.3:6: And the tongue is a fire, a universe of iniquity. The tongue is established among our members, which stains the whole body and inflames the wheel of our birth, itself inflamed by Gehenna.
verses.3:7: For every nature of beasts and of birds and of reptiles and of the rest is tamed and has been tamed by human nature,
verses.3:8: but no human being is able to tame the tongue: a restless evil, full of lethal poison.
verses.3:9: With it we bless God and the Father, and with it we curse people who have been made after the likeness of God.
verses.3:10: From the same mouth proceed blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to happen in this way.
verses.3:11: Does a spring pour forth sweet and bitter water from the same opening?
verses.3:12: Can a fig tree, my brothers, produce grapes, or a vine figs? So neither can salt water produce sweet water.
verses.3:13: Who is wise and disciplined among you? Let him show his work from good conduct in the gentleness of wisdom.
verses.3:14: Now if you have bitter jealousy, and contentions are in your hearts, do not boast and be liars against the truth;
verses.3:15: for this wisdom is not one descending from above, but is earthly, natural, diabolical.
verses.3:16: For where there is jealousy and contention, there is instability and every wicked work.
verses.3:17: But the wisdom that is from above is first indeed chaste, then peaceable, modest, open to persuasion, consenting to what is good, full of mercy and good fruits, not judging, without pretense.
verses.3:18: And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace for those who make peace.
verses.4:1: Where do wars and quarrels among you come from? Is it not from here: from your cravings, which do battle in your members?
verses.4:2: You crave and do not have; you kill and are jealous, and you cannot obtain; you quarrel and wage war, and you do not have, because you do not ask.
verses.4:3: You ask and do not receive, because you ask wrongly, so that you may spend it on your cravings.
verses.4:4: Adulterers, do you not know that friendship with this world is an enemy of God? Therefore whoever wishes to be a friend of this age is made an enemy of God.
verses.4:5: Or do you think that Scripture says in vain, "The spirit that dwells in you craves to the point of envy"?
verses.4:6: But He gives greater grace. For this reason it says, "God resists the proud, but to the humble He gives grace."
verses.4:7: Therefore be subject to God, but resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
verses.4:8: Draw close to God, and He will draw close to you. Cleanse your hands, sinners, and purify your hearts, you who are double-minded.
verses.4:9: Be wretched, and mourn, and weep; let your laughter be changed into mourning, and joy into grief.
verses.4:10: Humble yourselves in the Lord's sight, and He will exalt you.
verses.4:11: Do not speak ill of one another, brothers. The one who speaks ill of a brother, or who judges his brother, speaks ill of the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law, but a judge.
verses.4:12: There is one lawgiver and judge, who is able to destroy and to deliver.
verses.4:13: But who are you, who judge your neighbor? Look now, you who say, "Today or tomorrow we will go into that city, and indeed spend a year there, and trade, and make a profit,"
verses.4:14: you who do not know what will be tomorrow.
verses.4:15: For what is your life? It is a vapor appearing for a little while, and afterward it will be done away with; instead of your saying, "If the Lord wills," and, "If we live, we will do this or that."
verses.4:16: But now you exult in your pride. All such exultation is evil.
verses.4:17: Therefore, for the one who knows to do good and does not do it, it is sin for him.
verses.5:1: Come now, you rich, weep, howling over your miseries that will come upon you.
verses.5:2: Your riches have rotted, and your garments have been eaten by moths.
verses.5:3: Your gold and silver have rusted, and their rust will be a testimony against you, and it will eat your flesh like fire. You have stored up wrath for yourselves in the last days.
verses.5:4: Look, the pay of the workers who reaped your fields, which was fraudulently withheld by you, cries out, and their cry has entered into the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth.
verses.5:5: You have feasted on the earth, and in luxury you have nourished your hearts in the day of slaughter.
verses.5:6: You have condemned and killed the righteous one, and he does not resist you.
verses.5:7: Be patient, therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Look, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, enduring patiently until he receives the early and the late.
verses.5:8: Therefore, you also be patient, and strengthen your hearts, for the coming of the Lord has drawn near.
verses.5:9: Do not groan against one another, brothers, so that you may not be judged. Look, the judge stands before the door.
verses.5:10: Take, brothers, the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord as an example of an evil outcome, of hardship, and of patience.
verses.5:11: Look, we call blessed those who have endured. You have heard of the endurance of Job, and you have seen the end of the Lord, for the Lord is merciful and compassionate.
verses.5:12: But above all, my brothers, swear neither by heaven, nor by earth, nor any other oath whatever. Rather, let your speech be, "Yes, yes; No, no," so that you may not fall under judgment.
verses.5:13: Is anyone among you sorrowful? Let him pray. Is he of a contented mind? Let him sing psalms.
verses.5:14: Is anyone among you sick? Let him bring in the elders of the church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord.
verses.5:15: And the prayer of faith will save the sick one, and the Lord will lift him up; and if he is in sins, they will be forgiven him.
verses.5:16: Therefore confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, so that you may be saved; for the continual petition of a righteous person has great power.
verses.5:17: Elijah was a man like us, subject to suffering, and with prayer he prayed that it would not rain on the earth, and it did not rain for three years and six months.
verses.5:18: And he prayed again, and the sky gave rain, and the earth gave its fruit.
verses.5:19: My brothers, if anyone among you strays from the truth and someone turns him back,
verses.5:20: he ought to know that the one who causes a sinner to turn back from the error of his way will save his soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.

notes.1:2: Latin tentatio (like Greek peirasmos) covers both 'trial/testing' and 'temptation,' linking the trials of vv. 2 and 12 with the temptation to evil in vv. 13-14.
notes.1:4: The Clementine Vulgate reads the indicative habet ('has'), whereas the Greek reads the imperative ('let ... have').
notes.1:12: The Vulgate explicitly supplies Deus ('God') as the subject of repromisit ('promised'), whereas the earliest Greek witnesses leave the subject unexpressed.
notes.1:13: The Vulgate converts the quotation to third-person indirect speech (tentatur, 'he is tempted') rather than first-person direct speech, and renders Greek apeirastos kakon ('cannot be tempted by evil') with the active Latin coinage intentator malorum ('no tempter of evils').
notes.1:18: The Vulgate translates Greek aparche ('firstfruits') as initium ('beginning') and adds enim ('For').
notes.2:4: The Vulgate translates Greek diekrithete ('made distinctions') with judicatis ('pass judgment'), creating a wordplay with judices ('judges').
notes.2:15: The Clementine Vulgate reads frater et soror ('a brother and a sister'), whereas the Greek reads 'a brother or a sister.'
notes.2:18: The extent of the speaker's quotation is debated and may continue to the end of the verse. The Vulgate's sine operibus ('without works') agrees with the critical Greek text, whereas the Byzantine Greek tradition reads 'by your works.'
notes.2:20: The Vulgate reads mortua est ('is dead'), following the Byzantine Greek text rather than the Alexandrian reading 'useless/idle.'
notes.3:1: The Vulgate reads the second-person present sumitis ('you receive'), whereas the Greek reads the first-person future ('we will receive').
notes.3:7: The Vulgate reads et ceterorum ('and of the rest'), whereas the Greek reads 'and of sea creatures.'
notes.3:9: The Vulgate reads Deum et Patrem ('God and the Father'), agreeing with the Byzantine Greek text rather than the Alexandrian reading 'the Lord and Father.'
notes.3:12: The Vulgate reads uvas ('grapes'), whereas the Greek reads 'olives.'
notes.3:17: The Clementine text reads bonus consentiens, a transmitted variant of bonis consentiens ('consenting to what is good'), a phrase not present in Greek; the Vulgate also renders Greek adiakritos ('impartial') literally as non judicans ('not judging').
notes.4:4: The Vulgate reads masculine "Adulteri" ("Adulterers", whereas the critical Greek text has feminine "adulteresses"), uses "inimica" ("an enemy") rather than "enmity", and varies "hujus mundi" ("this world") with "sæculi hujus" ("this age").
notes.4:5: A famously debated verse: the Latin "spiritus qui habitat in vobis" ("the spirit that dwells in you", differing from the critical Greek "which he made to dwell in us") is understood by some interpreters as the human spirit inclined toward envy and by others as God's Spirit jealously longing for believers' devotion.
notes.4:12: The Clementine Vulgate places "But who are you, who judge your neighbor?" at the start of 4:13 (with 4:14 containing only "you who do not know what will be tomorrow" and 4:15 beginning with "For what is your life?"), and reads "to destroy and to deliver" ("perdere et liberare") in reverse of the Greek order.
notes.4:15: Unlike the Greek single conditional, the Clementine Vulgate divides the saying into two conditions ("Si Dominus voluerit. Et: Si vixerimus, faciemus...") and uses the future passive "exterminabitur" ("will be done away with").
notes.5:3: The Clementine Vulgate explicitly includes "vobis iram" ("wrath for yourselves", echoing Romans 2:5), whereas the Greek text reads simply "you have stored up treasure in the last days."
notes.5:4: "Sabaoth" (Latin "sabbaoth") preserves the transliterated Hebrew title meaning "hosts" or "armies." The Vulgate also reads "clamor eorum" ("their cry") rather than the Greek "the cries of the harvesters."
notes.5:7: Latin "temporaneum et serotinum" ("the early and the late") omits an explicit noun; it is traditionally understood to refer to the early (autumn) and late (spring) rains needed for the crop.
notes.5:10: The Clementine Vulgate has a distinctive three-part list—"exitus mali, laboris, et patientiæ" ("of an evil outcome, of hardship, and of patience")—where the Greek text has two terms ("of suffering and of patience").
notes.5:16: The Vulgate reads "ut salvemini" ("so that you may be saved") rather than the Greek "so that you may be healed," and "assidua" ("continual") for the Greek participle meaning "working" or "effective."
